_comment: How rtc-ship.sh ships motion-pipeline (plain Python app, run-to-completion 1.6.2 wiring added 2026-11-18). The release asset is a DETERMINISTIC git-archive tarball (.rtc/pre-package.sh); the auto-generated GitHub tag tarball is not byte-stable, and the tap formula pins its sha256 (.rtc/post-release.sh bumps the tap and pushes it — for the tap, merging IS shipping).
_comment_tests: How this repo's tests run is the repo's business (rtc-ship 1.6.2): the worktree's own venv has the runtime deps (textual, numpy, pillow, pytest-asyncio); the PATH/pipx pytest does NOT even import motion_pipeline. NO -m 'not slow': the slow render tests self-skip with a printed reason when the toolchain is absent and gate for real when it is present (the unfiltered run is what exposed the MP_PYTHON bug).
_comment_flaky: Load-sensitive TUI/PTY/venv tests carry @pytest.mark.flaky and run in their own low-parallelism shard from .rtc/pre-flight.sh (2026-11-21: four gates died on rotating load flakes). Main gate: not flaky. Never call a provider API from tests outside the rate limiter — test_no_external_api_calls.py enforces it.
_comment_versions: rtc_version_surface.py has no reader for a .py file or a PEP 621 [project] table (its toml-package kind is scoped to [package]), so pyproject.toml and motion_pipeline/__init__.py are NOT tool-bumped surfaces: tests/test_version_consistency.py pins VERSION == release-manifest.json == pyproject.toml == __init__.py == CHANGELOG top, so an incomplete bump fails the suite gate instead of shipping drifted.
